Friends of St Francis de Sales Catholic Infant and Junior School
The Friends of St Francis de Sales Catholic Infant and Junior School is the parent/staff association (PSA) for our school. All parents and guardians of children at the school, and all staff are automatically members of the PSA.
Our purpose is to enhance the quality of the children’s education and school life. We do this by raising money to help the school to cover costs for enrichment activities and resources that are not covered by the school budget. To this end, we organise a variety of fundraising events throughout the year for parents, children and staff.
We are a registered charity (Reg. Charity No. 1112318), regulated by the Charity Commission. We have a formal constitution and hold regular meetings throughout the year to plan our activities. All PSA members are warmly welcome to come along.
If you would like to find out more about joining the PSA, or if you have any questions, suggestions or feedback, you can email us at psa@sfds.haringey.sch.uk
International Summer Fayre
We would like to extend a heartfelt thank you to everyone who supported our Summer Fayre. It was a fantastic afternoon, and we are incredibly grateful to our parents, families, staff, volunteers, and businesses for helping to make the event such a success. We raised over £3.8k!
A special thank you goes to the many businesses and individuals who generously donated their time, prizes and resources. Your kindness and community spirit made a real difference and helped us raise valuable funds that will benefit our pupils.

Our Mission and Values
Our Mission and Values
At St. Francis de Sales Catholic Infant and Junior Schools Federation we attempt to follow the guidance given to us by St Francis, who said, “Be who you are and be that well.” As a Catholic school, we encourage our children to be unique, creative, open-minded and independent individuals, respectful of themselves and of others in our school, our local community and the wider world. We seek to develop the whole person and to nurture our children on their journey through life so they can grow into safe, caring, democratic, responsible and tolerant adults who make a positive difference to the wider community.
This philosophy gives rise to our mission statement…
At St Francis de Sales every child will achieve their own personal excellence by making outstanding progress in their academic, social and spiritual development. This will enable them to excel at secondary school and then attend a further educational institution should they choose.
Children have an entitlement to achieve well academically and at the same time to grow in equal measure in understanding Gospel values and living a rewarding Catholic life. The aim for our children is that when they leave Y6, they are equipped to excel at secondary school and build the foundation for success in the world of post compulsory education. When they arrive in society with positions of power and authority, they will be prepared for those positions by our five values instilled in them during their time at the school.
In striving to be extraordinary we will...
In striving to engage joyfully in our work we will...
In striving to be respectful we will...
In striving to show resilience we will...
In striving to work collaboratively we will...
In addition to the school's focus on these values for learning, in November 2014 the Department for Education published guidance on promoting British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. All schools have a duty to ‘actively promote’ the fundamental British values of: • Democracy• The rule of law• Individual liberty• Mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs and for those without faith Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural
At St. Francis De Sales, we put SMSC (Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural) education at the heart of school development; thinking about the people we aspire to be, the world we aspire to create and the education we aspire to provide. It encompasses personal development across the whole curriculum.
Through our 5 core values, we encourage students to accept responsibility for their behaviour, show initiative, and to understand how they can contribute positively to the life of the school and the wider society.
The children develop their respect and awareness of democracy here in St. Francis when they participate in the democratic process by annually voting for School Council representatives. We also have Digital Leaders, Faith Ambassadors and Reading Champions who promote and develop other aspects of school life.
Through our wide and varied extra-curricular clubs, visits and activities, we enable students to develop their self-knowledge, self-esteem, self-confidence and respect for others.
Our RHE curriculum and robust behaviour systems ensure that the children understand the difference between right and wrong and how this can relate to the Rule of Law in England.
In our culturally diverse school community, we enable students to have an appreciation and respect for their own and others’ cultures through school visits and celebrations within school.

Our School
Welcome
St Francis de Sales school has been a three-form entry federated infant and junior school (a federation means that the infant and junior schools used to be separate schools – but now the two schools are united under one headteacher). However. over recent years pupil numbers have been going down across London and we have reduced our pupil intake from three classes in each year group to two classes in each year group. We serve a community of nearly 500 pupils from nursery to year 6.At St Francis every child is encouraged to discover and nurture their God-given ability through a stimulating curriculum. Our aim is to engage and inspire our pupils by going beyond the restrictions of the national curriculum – producing youngsters who can take up their place in secondary education and the world of work with the knowledge and confidence they need to be successful.
For more information about what we teach and how we teach it, refer to our curriculum statement here.
As a Catholic school, our overall goal is to fulfil the Church’s mission in education by ensuring we provide the highest level of academic achievement in a moral and spiritual framework. So, at St Francis, we aim to have a school where;
To accomplish these aims, we strive to follow the guidance of St Francis himself, who said;
“Be who you are and be that well.”
This motivates everyone at the school to be the best that we can be and this is reflected in our mission statement;
“At St Francis de Sales every child will achieve their own personal excellence by making outstanding progress in their academic, social and spiritual development. This will enable them to excel at secondary school and then attend a further educational institution should they choose.”
Underpinning everything we do are our values – the core principles which drive our behaviours at all times. It is our strong belief that pupils who are aspirational, respectful, resilient, engaged, team-players will be successful in anything they choose to do.
Not only will you see our values prominently displayed throughout our school (there are some examples below), but you will notice how the values shine through in the behaviour of our pupils. In fact the behaviour in our school has been judged by Ofsted to be outstanding for the last decade.
We also ensure our pupils understand wider ‘British values’ – these are democracy, the rule of law, liberty, mutual respect and tolerance. These British values link very closely to our school values and they are promoted through all elements of the school curriculum, systems and processes.
Our values also support in our school’s statutory Prevent Duty. This is the duty the government has given all schools to ensure that we challenge any extreme view or ideology.
For more information on our values and how we promote them, please refer to our ‘Promoting British Values Policy here and on our Prevent Duty here.
In striving to be extraordinary we will...
In striving to engage joyfully in our work we will...
In striving to be respectful we will...
In striving to show resilience we will...
In striving to work collaboratively we will...
As an infant and junior school federation, we still have two inspections. The Infant School was judged to be 'good' with outstanding leadership and behaviour by Ofsted most recently in May 2024 (see here) and the junior school was judged to be ‘good’ with outstanding leadership and behaviour by Ofsted in May 2021 (see here).
Particularly pleasing comments from past inspections have included;
“Under the inspirational leadership of the headteacher, this school is going from strength to strength. He has embedded a culture of high aspiration for all within a caring faith ethos.”
“Leadership is outstanding. The executive headteacher, head of school and deputy headteacher are highly ambitious for all pupils. They have created a culture of ‘no excuses’ and high expectations, and these are part and parcel of everyday school life. “
"Behaviour is outstanding. Pupils look after each other and unkindness is not tolerated. Pupils’ are extremely respectful, polite and courteous. They feel safe and are very well cared for. Leaders provide excellent opportunities for pupils’ personal development. Pupils display exceptionally strong attitudes to learning."
"Pupils’ welfare is at the heart of the school’s work."
"Pupils believe that they can achieve great things if they work hard and apply themselves well to their work. One pupil said, ‘Children from Tottenham don’t often go to university but we will."
"The atmosphere of aspiration which pervades the school is as strong among the staff team as it is among pupils. As a result, teaching has improved and teachers are keen to develop their skills even further."
The school is also Inspected by the Catholic School Inspectorate, with the last inspection in October 2024 judging the Catholic life of the school to be outstanding and stating;
'There is a joyful, inclusive and welcoming ethos at St Francis De Sales which is celebrated by the whole school community as they strive to follow the school motto ‘Be who you are and be that well.'
'The school’s work with the local parish is exemplary and the impact on outcomes for the pupils is evident in lessons, in worship and in Catholic life and mission.'
'Pastoral care for pupils is outstanding.'

Lux Mundi Catholic Academy Consultation
Lux Mundi Catholic Academy
Introduction to Our Academy Consultation Process
Welcome to this dedicated consultation page for the St Francis de Sales Catholic Federation. We are entering a period of reflection and dialogue as we consider the possibility of academisation and joining Lux Mundi, an established and growing Catholic academy trust.
In an ever-evolving educational landscape, schools face increasing challenges—including falling pupil numbers, financial pressures and curriculum demands. In light of these, it is essential that we take proactive steps to secure the long-term success of our schools and the pupils we serve. Joining a wider family of Catholic schools offers us an opportunity to strengthen our mission, protect our Catholic identity, and work collaboratively with like-minded communities who share our values and vision.This move is not taken lightly. It comes from a place of deep care and commitment to our children, families and staff. We firmly believe that becoming part of the Lux Mundi Catholic Academy Trust will enhance the quality of Catholic education we provide, support strong academic outcomes and enable the young people of the St Francis de Sales Federation to continue to flourish—spiritually, academically, and socially.
The stakeholders' consultation is now closed. Please see the Consultation Report below.

Extended Day Provision
Extended Day Provision
At St Francis de Sales School, we are delighted to be able to offer a breakfast club, a wide range of after school clubs and an extended day provision for our children. We appreciate that there are a great many demands on parents' time, and other commitments do not always fit neatly around school hours.
After School Club 3.15pm to 4.15pm
We offer an extended day for those parents who require childcare outside of the regular school hours. This service is provided at the school by Awesome Childcare.
Please call Sandra Lawrence on 079215 26877
Open Monday to Friday

Reading
Our reading ambassadors are passionate about reading and love to talk about the books that they enjoy. We have reading ambassadors from Year 2 to Year 6. They are keen to share their favourite books with others and are committed to helping every pupil in our school develop a love of reading. A reading ambassador promotes the love of reading across our school. They do this by; running school reading and writing competitions, finding out our pupils’ reading preferences to help us keep our library engaging, support reading events such as World Book Day and author visits, offering book recommendations to others and supporting pupils to develop their reading skills.
